# Where the evidence is thin

A reviewer goes for the weakest number first. This finds them before that happens, by walking the artifacts behind each headline claim and counting what actually sits underneath.

None of this says a result is wrong. Some of these are perfectly sound and the report says which. What it will not do is let a number with three races behind it read the same as one with sixty.

## 1. The cheap-stop threshold

The edge sits at **22.5 s** because one race puts it there: IMSA GTD at indianapolis in 2025. The next tyre-limited race is IMSA GTD at watkins_glen 2025, at 13.2 s — so removing one race moves the threshold by 41%.

The **rule** is not thin: 150 race-seasons sit above the edge and none of them is tyre-limited, across every class. It is the constant that rests on one race, and a bootstrap cannot fix that — the statistic is a maximum, so it sits on the boundary of its own support.

**Already stated** in `when_tyres_beat_fuel.md`, `synthesis.md` and the paper. Quote the rule; treat the number as an order of magnitude.

## 2. Transfer scores built on two folds

Every headline transfer number is a mean over leave-one-race-out folds. How many folds, and how far apart they sit:

| circuit-class | published mean | folds | the folds themselves | spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lime Rock GTD | **+0.573** | 3 | +0.564, +0.567, +0.588 | 0.024 |
| Lime Rock GTDPRO | **+0.497** | 2 | +0.357, +0.638 | 0.281 |
| Laguna Seca GTD | **+0.273** | 6 | +0.439, +0.382, +0.283, +0.039, +0.098, +0.396 | 0.400 |
| Laguna Seca GTDPRO | **+0.256** | 5 | +0.386, +0.255, -0.029, +0.282, +0.385 | 0.415 |
| Bahrain HYPERCAR | **+0.217** | 4 | +0.049, +0.310, +0.266, +0.243 | 0.261 |

**Lime Rock GTDPRO is the weak one.** Its +0.497 is the mean of 2 folds that run +0.357 to +0.638 — a spread of 0.281, which is larger than most circuit-classes' entire score. It should not be quoted beside a number averaged over five or six folds without saying so.

The neighbouring Lime Rock GTD figure is a different case: three folds sitting within 0.024 of each other. Same circuit, same protocol, far more stable — which is itself worth knowing, since it says the instability is not a property of the circuit alone.

## 3. Circuits with almost no data behind their constants

The project quotes a **14-fold** track-position range from monaco to las_vegas. The high end rests on **3 races** at a circuit first run in 2023; the low end on 4.

Circuits whose constants come from fewer than 4 observations:

| circuit | degradation races | track-position races | SC editions |
|---|---|---|---|
| imola | 3 | 3 | — |
| interlagos | 3 | — | — |
| las_vegas | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| losail | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| melbourne | 3 | — | — |
| ricard | 1 | 1 | — |
| shanghai | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| suzuka | 3 | — | — |

**ricard is the extreme case**: its degradation coefficients come from 1 race, and its track-position constant from one too. Both feed the simulator like any other circuit's, and neither is a measurement in the sense the others are.

The safety-car layer handles this correctly already — a Jeffreys prior and a credible interval, so a circuit with three editions gets a wide band rather than false precision. Monaco's much-quoted 0.44 carries an interval of [0.14, 0.77] for exactly this reason, and the width is as much the result as the point.

The degradation and track-position layers do not do the same thing. They report a per-circuit constant with a cluster-robust interval on the *slope*, which says nothing about how few races produced it.

## What is not thin

Worth stating, so the list above is not read as a general disclaimer.

The decision audit rests on 1,280 replayed stops and the baseline comparison on 1,263 of them, both under one criterion. The pit-loss correlation is computed across 205 race-seasons and its interval is bootstrapped over races rather than over the six class summaries. The transfer difference between GT3 and prototype classes uses 51 circuit-classes with a permutation test alongside the bootstrap. Those four are the load-bearing results and none of them turns on a handful of races.
